item.title: Archdiocese of New York agrees to $800 million settlement over sexual abuse claims
item.description: The 1,300 survivors of sexual abuse by clergy members and lay workers have all agreed to the settlement, according to an attorney for some of the plaintiffs.

item.title: Texas voters cast early ballots in key senate race
item.description: In Texas, early voting is underway. The state's tight race for U.S. Senate will ultimately help decide the balance of power in Washington.

item.title: Comedian Charlie Berens has made Wisconsin politics a laughing matter
item.description: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer speaks with comedian and former journalist Charlie Berens. His comedy blends political satire with a distinctly Wisconsin sense of humor.

item.description: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer speaks with Sam Woods and Joy Powers, hosts of WUWM's Swing State of the Union podcast, about the top issues for voters in the swing state of Wisconsin.

item.title: How data centers became a bipartisan political issue in Wisconsin
item.description: Data centers are a big issue across the country. As midterms approach, many look to the swing state of Wisconsin for lessons for how that issue could play out nationally.

item.title: U.S. birth rate drops to record low, but older women are having more babies
item.description: The U.S. birth rate fell to its lowest level ever recorded, according to a report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The drop would have been greater, but women over age 30 are having more children.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Flooding in Four Corners region displaces residents, as storms move southeast
item.description: Intense rainfall slammed the Four Corners region late this week. As rivers flooded, towns declared evacuations and emergencies and made rescues.

item.title: Father who killed the Bend school shooter speaks to Oregon Public Broadcasting
item.description: Kaylub Giamanco, the father who shot the 16-year-old who opened fire on a Bend, Ore., elementary school and killed three kids and a teacher, shares what he wants people to know about his experience.

item.title: The Pentagon's guidelines for "responsible AI" aren't always followed, report shows
item.description: The Pentagon is building weapons and projects with AI capabilities that officials say don't always closely adhere to the agency's own guidelines for AI, according to a congressional watchdog report published in October.
